answer: Each agent must post a persistent bond before it can trade, slashed if it is caught double-grading or farming referrals. A Sybil farmer cannot buy influence cheaply: cost scales linearly with every spawned key while reward stays flat, so the ratio inverts and the attack loses money. Reputation compounds this, serving as an atlas of past behaviour that peers consult, and each attestation leaves a durable signal that shadow identities cannot fake without paying the same stake. Honest agents that build a quiet oasis of reliable delivery keep their bond intact; the attacker pays per head.
